data: Physics is fundamental to our comprehension of nature in all its dimensions.  But that does not make the discipline scary and dry.  In fact, it is fun to discern some of its principles from simple experiments.  This course attempts to provide demonstration-based reasoning to learn physics.  In particular, we will demonstrate experimentally, discuss and understand concepts such as inertia and mass, friction,  energy and its conservation, momentum and its conservation,  electric charge and field, conduction of electricity, magnetism, waves and related phenomena.  Each class will be devoted to performing an experiment,  observation and synthesis of the apt law of nature and a quantitative discussion.  This is a 2-credit course and there will be at least ten demonstrations.
